## Appearance

Agatha Sowerby is a stout woman who weighs two hundred pounds. She possesses a heavy body, and her movement is characterized by a perpetual waddle.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER IX. Mrs. Agatha Sowerby Is Properly Horrified P31](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0031), [v1 CHAPTER XXXVIII. The Bend in the Road P30](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0030), [v1 CHAPTER XXXVIII. The Bend in the Road P31](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0031)_

## Personality

Agatha Sowerby is a kindly, cheerful, and industrious woman who thoroughly enjoys being consulted for guidance. Marked by strong piety, she views horse racing and drama as sinful, and she entirely disbelieves in higher education for women. Though well-intentioned, she is somewhat meddlesome, boastful, and prone to speaking her mind too freely. She takes pride in voicing her opinions without fear or partiality, though her critical nature often leads her to find fault in others. Additionally, she is a passionate political partisan who possesses remarkable foresight. Her practical talents include dressmaking and preparing raspberry cordial.

## History

Mrs. Agatha Sowerby first took notice when [Obed Abernethy](../character/obed-abernethy.md) left town in his buggy, later visiting [Thirza Abernethy](../character/thirza-abernethy.md) at [Grey Shutters](../codex/places.md#grey-shutters) to express strong doubts upon learning he was adopting an orphan child. During a subsequent visit, she rudely mocked the young girl Nell's plain appearance and red hair, provoking an enraged outburst from [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md). [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) later visited her house to deliver a humble, dramatic apology, which Mrs. Sowerby accepted with forgiveness. When [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) later refused to return to school after an incident, [Thirza](../character/thirza-abernethy.md) sought advice from Mrs. Sowerby, who recommended allowing the girl to rest at home until her temper subsided. [Obed](../character/obed-abernethy.md) eventually enlisted Mrs. Sowerby's help to buy fabric and sew a stylish new gown with puffed sleeves as a [Christmas](../codex/places.md#merry-christmas) gift for [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md). Over time, Mrs. Sowerby's initial misgivings faded, leading her to compliment Nell's growth and grace.

## Quotes

> "However, I had a bit of a scare that you might not be, seeing Obed head out earlier today. My thought was that perhaps he was heading to the doctor’s office."
>
> — Agatha Sowerby — [v1 CHAPTER I. Mrs. Agatha Sowerby Is Surprised P14](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0014)

> "I simply reckon she has succeeded, and I would certainly not hold back from stating as much. You bring honor to your companions, Nell, indeed you do, and every one of us is proud of you."
>
> — Agatha Sowerby — [v1 CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out P48](../source/v01-c32.md#nw-v01-c32-p0048)

> "I’m not aware of it. My assumption is that your teaching will take place directly here in Brierley. You have been selected by the trustees to receive the school."
>
> — Agatha Sowerby — [v1 CHAPTER XXXVIII. The Bend in the Road P36](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0036)

> "She’s awfully thin and plain, Thirza. Step over this way, child, so I can inspect you. Goodness gracious, has anyone ever witnessed such freckles? And hair that is as red as carrots! Step over this way, child, I tell you."
>
> — Agatha Sowerby — [v1 CHAPTER IX. Mrs. Agatha Sowerby Is Properly Horrified P14](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0014)

> "Child, yes, it frightens me. Observe his expression. You will understand its meaning once you’ve witnessed that expression as frequently as I have."
>
> — Agatha Sowerby — [v1 CHAPTER XXXVII. The Reaper Whose Name Is Death P7](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0007)

## Relationships

### [Nell Harcourt](../character/nell-harcourt.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/agatha-sowerby--nell-harcourt.md)

Agatha and [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) get off to a rocky start when Agatha visits [Grey Shutters](../codex/places.md#grey-shutters) and openly mocks Nell's plain looks and red hair, provoking [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) into a violent temper. After [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) is persuaded to deliver a dramatic apology at Agatha's home, Agatha forgives the girl and gives her encouragement regarding her hair. Later, Agatha acts as an advisor to Nell's guardian, recommending that [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) be allowed to rest at home after a violent schoolhouse outburst.

### [Thirza Abernethy](../character/thirza-abernethy.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/agatha-sowerby--thirza-abernethy.md)
